notification.title: Device security issues
notification.failing: Your device has security issues. Click to fix them or contact {{contact}}.
notification.warning:
⚠️ Your device is not securely configured.

In {{days}} days your access will be blocked.

Click to fix issues now or contact {{contact}}.
notification.blocking: ⚠️ Your device is insecure and your access has been blocked. Click to fix issues or contact {{contact}}.

reuse.title: Possible Phishing Alert
reuse.message:
You are using the password of the user {{username}} for {{system}}, to connect to another site.

⚠️ This may be a phishing attack: verify that this is the site you think it is.

If it is; re-use of passwords is dangerous, and not allowed.

quality.number-uppercase: Must contain at least {{min}} uppercase letter(s)
quality.number-lowercase: Must contain at least {{min}} lowercase letter(s)
quality.entropy: Does not have enough different characters
quality.username-password: Must not be based on the username
quality.reuse: Must not reuse the password of '{{label}}'
quality.profile-separation: Must not be stored in external profile '{{profile}}'

notification.title: Account security issues
notification.failing: One of your accounts has security issues. Click to fix them or contact {{contact}}.
notification.warning:
⚠️ One of your accounts is not securely configured.

In {{days}} days your access will be blocked.

Click to fix issues now or contact {{contact}}.
notification.blocking: ⚠️ One of your accounts is not securely configured. Your access has been blocked. Click to fix issues or contact {{contact}}.

messaging.please-contact: Unable to connect to native application. Please contact {{contact}}

first-connect.warning:
Connection to {{hostname}} requires Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).

⚠️ You will be disconnected in {{minutes}} minutes if you do not configure your account to use MFA, such as a Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP).

Contact {{contact}} if you need help.
first-connect.disconnected:
You have been disconnected from {{domain}} because you connected to {{hostname}} without Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).

Reconnect and configure your account to use MFA, such as a Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP).

Contact {{contact}} if you need help.

session-expiration.warning:
You have to periodically reconnect to {{hostname}} using Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).

⚠️ You will be disconnected in {{minutes}} minutes if you do not do not reconnect.
session-expiration.disconnected: You have been disconnected from {{domain}} because you did not reconnect to {{hostname}} using Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).

block-page.page-blocked-text: The website you are trying to visit is blocked for security reasons.
block-page.security-analysis: To understand why the page was blocked, please refer to the security analysis.
block-page.request-exception: If you are sure there is no security issue you can request a temporary exception
block-page.provide-reason: Please provide your reason for requesting an exception
block-page.request-submitted-popup: Your exception request has been submitted. You can now access the site.

block-modal.request-exception: In urgent and exceptional cases you can request an exception if you are blocked.
block-modal.provide-reason: Please provide your reason for requesting an exception

warn.title: Unmanaged application (shadow IT)
warn.message: Be careful not to share confidential or company data with {{hostname}}, and contact {{contact}} if you need an approved alternative.

clickfix.title: Possible scam detected
clickfix.message:
Something just copied a computer command to your clipboard. Scammers use this trick ("ClickFix") to get you to paste and run harmful commands, for example in PowerShell, the Windows Run dialog, or a terminal.

⚠️ Do not paste it unless you are certain it is safe.

Click for more information and contact {{contact}} if you are unsure.

leaking.title: Possible secret leakage
leaking.message:
You have transferred information that looks like a secret (such as a password or API key):

{{examples}}

{{sanitizeMode}}
leaking.manual-sanitize: If this was an accident, remove the secrets and perform the operation again.
leaking.automated-sanitize: If this was an accident, click to sanitize the clipboard and then paste again.

disable-modal.title: Dangerous Extension
disable-modal.message-install: A potentially dangerous extension was found and has been deactivated.
disable-modal.message-update: An extension was deactivated because an update increased its risk. Do not reactivate it without understanding the risk.
disable-modal.message-error: The extension could not be analyzed because

status.error-store: unable to analyze the extension store page

install-blocked.blacklist-category: the category it belongs to has been blacklisted
install-blocked.risk-global: the overall risk level is too high or unknown
install-blocked.risk-impact: the risk of its access to sensitive data is too high or unknown
install-blocked.risk-likelihood: the probability that it is malware or can be hacked is too high or unknown
install-blocked.not-verified: neither the extension nor its publisher are verified by the extension store
install-blocked.poor-rating: it was rated poorly or insufficiently
install-blocked.all-domains: it requests access to all traffic using '{{example}}'
install-blocked.protected-domain: it requests access to protected domain '{{example}}'

block-page.request-exception: If you are sure the extension does not represent a security risk you can request a temporary exception
block-page.provide-reason: Please provide your reason for requesting an exception

webRequestBlocking.description: Allows the use of the chrome.webRequest API for blocking.
webRequestBlocking.analysis: Extensions with the webRequestBlocking permission, in conjunction with the webRequest, can block network requests (requires host permissions and only applicable to force-installed extensions).

accessibilityFeatures.modify.description: Lets extensions modify accessibility feature states when using the chrome.accessibilityFeatures API.

accessibilityFeatures.read.description: Lets extensions read accessibility states when using the chrome.accessibilityFeatures API.

activeTab.description: Gives temporary access to the active tab through a user gesture. For details, see activeTab.
activeTab.analysis: Extensions with the activeTab permission can temporarily access the active tab, including injecting scripts and modifying content, but only when explicitly invoked by a user gesture. Access is revoked when the user closes the tab or navigates away. Compared to <all_urls>, activeTab is safer as it does not grant persistent access.

alarms.description: Gives access to the chrome.alarms API.
alarms.analysis: Extensions with the alarms permission can schedule code to run periodically or at a specified time in the future.

audio.description: Gives access to the chrome.audio API.

background.description: Makes Chrome start up early (as soon as the user logs into their computer, before they launch Chrome), and shut down late (even after its last window is closed, until the user explicitly quits Chrome).
background.analysis: Extensions with the background permission can force the browser run invisibly as soon as the user logs in to the computer, and keep the browser running after the last window is closed (until the user explicitly quits).

bookmarks.description: Gives access to the chrome.bookmarks API.
bookmarks.analysis: Extensions with the bookmarks permission can create, organize, and otherwise manipulate bookmarks.

browsingData.description: Gives access to the chrome.browsingData API.
browsingData.analysis: Extensions with the browsingData permission can remove browsing data from a user's local profile, which could result in forensics / logging issues.

certificateProvider.description: Gives access to the chrome.certificateProvider API.

clipboardRead.description: Lets the extension paste items from the clipboard using the web platform Clipboard API.
clipboardRead.analysis: Extensions with the clipboardRead permission can read the system's clipboard content.

clipboardWrite.description: Lets the extension cut and copy items to the clipboard using the web platform Clipboard API.
clipboardWrite.analysis: Extensions with the clipboardWrite permission can modify the system's clipboard content.

contentSettings.description: Gives access to the chrome.contentSettings API.

contextMenus.description: Gives access to the chrome.contextMenus API.
contextMenus.analysis: Extensions with the contextMenus permission can add items to the browser's context menu (also known as the right-click menu).

cookies.description: Gives access to the chrome.cookies API.
cookies.analysis: Extensions with the cookies permission can retrieve and modify cookies (requires host permissions).

debugger.description: Gives access to the chrome.debugger API.
debugger.analysis: Extensions with the debugger permission have access to the browser's DevTools Protocol (CDP), enabling advanced debugging capabilities, including inspecting network interactions, debugging JavaScript, modifying the DOM and CSS, essentially providing super user access.

declarativeContent.description: Gives access to the chrome.declarativeContent API.
declarativeContent.analysis: Extensions with the declarativeContent permission can take actions depending on the content of a page, without requiring permission to read the page's content.

declarativeNetRequest.description: Gives access to the chrome.declarativeNetRequest API.
declarativeNetRequest.analysis: Extensions with the declarativeNetRequest permission can block network requests without requiring host permissions, and redirect requests and modify headers if it has host permissions.

declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess.description: Gives access to the chrome.declarativeNetRequest API but requires host permissions for all actions.

declarativeNetRequestFeedback.description: Gives permission to write errors and warnings to the DevTools console when using the chrome.declarativeNetRequest API. This permission is for use with unpacked extensions and is ignored for extensions installed from the Chrome Web Store.

desktopCapture.description: Gives access to the chrome.desktopCapture API.
desktopCapture.analysis: Extensions with the desktopCapture permission can capture the content of your entire screen, individual window or individual tab. desktopCapture needs to be invoked by a user gesture, unless the extension is force-installed, in which case in can capture the screen without user interaction.

dns.description: Gives access to the chrome.dns API.

documentScan.description: Gives access to the chrome.documentScan API.

downloads.description: Gives access to the chrome.downloads API.
downloads.analysis: Extensions with the downloads permission can programmatically initiate, monitor, manipulate, and search for downloads. This can be used to download scripts.

enterprise.deviceAttributes.description: Gives access to the chrome.enterprise.deviceAttributes API.

enterprise.hardwarePlatform.description: Gives access to the chrome.enterprise.hardwarePlatform API.

enterprise.networkingAttributes.description: Gives access to the chrome.enterprise.networkingAttributes API.

enterprise.platformKeys.description: Gives access to the chrome.enterprise.platformKeys API.

favicon.description: Grants access to the Favicon API.

fileBrowserHandler.description: Gives access to the chrome.fileBrowserHandler API.

fileSystemProvider.description: Gives access to the chrome.fileSystemProvider API.
fileSystemProvider.analysis: Extensions with the fileSystemProvider permission can create file systems that are accessible from the file manager (only applicable to ChromeOS).

fontSettings.description: Gives access to the chrome.fontSettings API.

gcm.description: Gives access to the chrome.gcm and chrome.instanceID APIs.

geolocation.description: Allows the extension to use the geolocation API without prompting the user for permission.

history.description: Gives access to the chrome.history API.
history.analysis: Extensions with the history permission can add, remove, and query for URLs in the browser's history.

identity.description: Gives access to the chrome.identity API.
identity.analysis: Extensions with the identity permission can prompt users to authenticate with their Google accounts using OAuth 2.0, but the user must approve the request for the extension to obtain an access token.

identity_email.description: Gives access to the user's email address through the chrome.identity API.

idle.description: Gives access to the chrome.idle API.
idle.analysis: Extensions with the idle permission can detect whether the machine is idle, in use, or locked.

loginState.description: Gives access to the chrome.loginState API.

management.description: Gives access to the chrome.management API.
management.analysis: Extensions with the management permission can manage your installed apps, extensions, and themes. If the extension is force-installed, it can disable other extensions.

nativeMessaging.description: Gives access to the native messaging API.
nativeMessaging.analysis: Extensions with the nativeMessaging permission can communicate with cooperating applications installed on the user's machine.

notifications.description: Gives access to the chrome.notifications API.
notifications.analysis: Extensions with the notifications permission can display notifications on the user's desktop.

offscreen.description: Gives access to the chrome.offscreen API.
offscreen.analysis: Use the offscreen API to create and manage offscreen documents.

pageCapture.description: Gives access to the chrome.pageCapture API, allowing programmatic export of HTML
pageCapture.analysis: Can be run without user interaction; extensions can silently copy everything that is visible on browsed pages.

platformKeys.description: Gives access to the chrome.platformKeys API.

power.description: Gives access to the chrome.power API.
power.analysis: Extensions with the power permission can override the system's power management features like preventing the device from sleeping and allowing the extension to run while the screen is off.

printerProvider.description: Gives access to the chrome.printerProvider API.

printing.description: Gives access to the chrome.printing API.

printingMetrics.description: Gives access to the chrome.printingMetrics API.

privacy.description: Gives access to the chrome.privacy API.
privacy.analysis: Extensions with the privacy permission can manage browser features that may affect user privacy and safety, for example turn off phishing protection (safeBrowsingEnabled).

processes.description: Gives access to the chrome.processes API.

proxy.description: Gives access to the chrome.proxy API.
proxy.analysis: Extensions with the proxy permission can configure how the user's internet traffic is routed, which can be exploited for data theft, man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks, phishing, and bypassing network security measures.

readingList.description: Gives access to the chrome.readingList API.

runtime.description: Gives access to runtime.connectNative() and runtime.sendNativeMessage(). For all other features of the runtime namespace, no permission is required.

scripting.description: Gives access to the chrome.scripting API.
scripting.analysis: Extensions with the scripting permission can inject and execute code in web pages, which can potentially be used for data exfiltration or session hijacking (requires host permissions).

search.description: Gives access to the chrome.search API.

sessions.description: Gives access to the chrome.sessions API.

sidePanel.description: Gives access to the chrome.sidePanel API.
sidePanel.analysis: Extensions with the sidePanel permission can display content in the browser's side panel alongside the main content of a webpage, enabling a persistent interface that complement the user's browsing journey.

storage.description: Gives access to the chrome.storage API.
storage.analysis: Extensions with the storage permission can store and retrieve user data, which can persist even after clearing the cache and browsing history.

system.cpu.description: Gives access to the chrome.system.cpu API.

system.display.description: Gives access to the chrome.system.display API.

system.memory.description: Gives access to the chrome.system.memory API.

system.storage.description: Gives access to the chrome.system.storage API.

tabCapture.description: Gives access to the chrome.tabCapture API.
tabCapture.analysis: Extensions with the tabCapture permission can capture the content of any tab. tabCapture needs to be invoked by a user gesture, unless the extension is force-installed, in which case in can capture the screen without user interaction.

tabGroups.description: Gives access to the chrome.tabGroups API.

tabs.description: Gives access to privileged fields of the Tab objects used by several APIs, including chrome.tabs and chrome.windows. You usually don't need to declare this permission to use those APIs.
tabs.analysis: Can see the URL and title of every tab you open and can redirect, close, or create tabs. Combined with broad host permissions, this enables full surveillance and control of your browsing. In MV2 this also gives 'scripting' permission.

topSites.description: Gives access to the chrome.topSites API.

tts.description: Gives access to the chrome.tts API.

ttsEngine.description: Gives access to the chrome.ttsEngine API.

unlimitedStorage.description: Provides an unlimited quota for chrome.storage.local, IndexedDB, Cache Storage, and Origin Private File System. For more information, see Storage and cookies.
unlimitedStorage.analysis: Extensions with the unlimitedStorage permission have no storage quota restrictions for chrome.storage.local, IndexedDB, Cache Storage, and the Origin Private File System.

userScripts.description: Gives access to the chrome.userScripts API. NOTE: the user must also explicitly enable the usage of user scripts.

vpnProvider.description: Gives access to the chrome.vpnProvider API.

wallpaper.description: Gives access to the chrome.wallpaper API.

webAuthenticationProxy.description: Gives access to the chrome.webAuthenticationProxy API.

webNavigation.description: Gives access to the chrome.webNavigation API.
webNavigation.analysis: Extensions with the webNavigation permission can track websites the user visits by listening to navigation events.

webRequest.description: Gives access to the chrome.webRequest API.
webRequest.analysis: Access to HTTP headers, including cookies, allowing the theft of session secrets.

<all_urls>.description: Grants the extension permission to operate on all http:// and https:// URLs in the browser.
<all_urls>.analysis: Extensions with the <all_urls> host permission (or equivalent patterns) can utilize their granted permissions on every website visited, greatly increasing the possibility for broad data collection or injection attacks.

controller.title: Who is responsible for my data
controller.body: The organisation responsible for the data described in this notice is {{org}}. {{org}} decided to deploy Citadel and configured how it operates on this device.

roles.title: Citadel's role
roles.body: Citadel is security software installed by {{org}}, not a service operated by its publisher. The publisher does not receive, store, or have access to any data produced by Citadel. Everything described below is sent only to systems operated by {{org}}.

changes.title: Will this notice change?
changes.body: {{org}} may update this notice if the configuration of Citadel changes. You will always see the version that reflects the current configuration of this device.

item.device: Basic security settings on this device, such as disk encryption and pending updates.
item.account: Whether corporate and sensitive third-party accounts follow password and multi-factor authentication requirements.
item.shadowit: Use of external applications not managed by {{org}} ("shadow IT").
item.dlp: Accidental disclosure of secrets or credentials in what you type or paste.
item.extension: Browser extensions, before they are installed or updated.

legal-basis.title: Legal basis
legal-basis.body: This processing is carried out in the context of your employment or engagement with {{org}}, on the basis of {{org}}'s legitimate interest in protecting its information systems, or in performance of your contract.

scope.title: Protected scope
scope.none: {{org}} has not restricted Citadel's protected scope to specific domains or applications in this configuration.
scope.all-accounts: all accounts used in the browser
scope.protected-only: restricted to third-party services within {{org}}'s protected scope
scope.no-restriction: not restricted to any particular list of services

account-scope.title: Which accounts are checked
account-scope.body: Account checks apply to {{scope}}, and are {{restriction}}.

recipients.title: Who receives this data
recipients.body: Citadel sends the results of these checks only to systems operated by {{org}} (e.g. its own security monitoring platform). Citadel's publisher never receives this data. Some checks rely on public threat-intelligence lists (e.g. known malicious domains or common secrets formats) that are downloaded by Citadel; nothing about your activity is sent to those sources.

retention.title: How long data is kept
retention.body: Security event data is kept in the browser for {{appDays}} days, account-related data for {{acctDays}} days, and session data for {{sessionDays}} days, after which it is deleted. Where this data is also sent to {{org}}'s security monitoring platform, it is retained there according to that platform's own retention policy, as configured by {{org}}.

security.title: Security
security.body: Citadel processes only the data necessary for the purposes above, and all communication with {{org}}'s systems is encrypted in transit. Any passwords or credentials Citadel evaluates are hashed and are never stored or transmitted in plain text.

data-collected.title: What data is collected
data-collected.body: The specific data points collected for each check above, and why, are {{link}}.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.intro: To exercise any of the following rights, contact {{org}}'s data protection contact: {{contact}}. Citadel's publisher cannot act on this request, as it does not hold your data.

item.access: Right of access : obtain a copy of the data {{org}} holds about you through Citadel.
item.rectification: Right to rectification : correct inaccurate or incomplete data.
item.erasure: Right to erasure : request deletion of your data, subject to {{org}}'s legal retention obligations.
item.restriction: Right to restriction : request that processing of your data be limited.
item.objection: Right to object : object to processing carried out on the basis of legitimate interest.
item.portability: Right to portability : receive data you provided in a machine-readable format.

rights.authority: You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the relevant data protection supervisory authority.
